body.en: Every quadratic can be solved — and when the discriminant is negative, the solutions live in the complex numbers. This chapter ties graphing, factoring and the imaginary unit together.
Define \( i=\sqrt{-1} \), so \( i^{2}=-1 \). A complex number has the form \( a+bi \) with \( a,b \) real; add and multiply just as with binomials, replacing \( i^{2} \) by \( -1 \).

body.en:
Describe the roots of \( x^{2}+2x+5=0 \).

Discriminant \( \Delta=2^{2}-4(1)(5)=-16<0 \), so there are no real roots — two complex conjugates. Solving:

\[ x=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{-16}}{2}=-1\pm 2i. \]

label.en: ▲ Algebra 2 Traps & Commandments — Quadratics & Complex Numbers

body.en:
• Powers of i Cycle: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\). For high powers \(i^n\), divide the exponent \(n\) by 4 and evaluate using the remainder (e.g. \(i^{27} = i^{4(6)+3} = i^3 = -i\)).
  • Multiplying Negative Radicals: Never write \(\sqrt{-3}\sqrt{-12} = \sqrt{36} = 6\)! You must extract the imaginary unit first: \((i\sqrt{3})(i\sqrt{12}) = i^2\sqrt{36} = -1(6) = -6\).
  • Discriminant Interpretation: For \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\): if \(\Delta > 0\), two distinct real roots; if \(\Delta = 0\), one repeated real rational root (vertex on \(x\)-axis); if \(\Delta < 0\), two non-real complex conjugate roots \(a \pm bi\).
  • Completing the Square with \(a \neq 1\): Always factor the leading coefficient \(a\) out of the quadratic and linear terms before adding \((b/(2a))^2\). In \(2x^2 - 12x\), factor to \(2(x^2 - 6x)\), then add 9 inside the parentheses (which actually adds \(2 \times 9 = 18\) to that side).

label.en: Worked Example C — Euclidean Distance & Orthogonal Projection

body.en:
A displacement has horizontal component \( \Delta x = 4 \) and vertical component \( \Delta y = 9 \). Find the squared magnitude \( d^2 \) and the area of the right triangle formed with the axes.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. By the Pythagorean theorem, \( d^2 = (4)^2 + (9)^2 = 16 + 81 = \mathbf{97} \).
  2. The enclosed right-triangle area is \( A = \frac{1}{2}(4)(9) = \mathbf{18} \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Euclidean Distance & Orthogonal Projection

body.en:
A displacement has horizontal component \( \Delta x = 5 \) and vertical component \( \Delta y = 5 \). Find the squared magnitude \( d^2 \) and the area of the right triangle formed with the axes.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. By the Pythagorean theorem, \( d^2 = (5)^2 + (5)^2 = 25 + 25 = \mathbf{50} \).
  2. The enclosed right-triangle area is \( A = \frac{1}{2}(5)(5) = \mathbf{12.5} \).

question.en: Solve \(x^2-4x+13=0\) and express roots in the form \(a\pm bi\).
Solve \(2x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\) by completing the square, expressing all solutions in exact \(a \pm bi\) form.

solution.en:
Divide by the leading coefficient 2 or factor it out from the variable terms:

\[2(x^2 - 3x) = -5 \implies x^2 - 3x = -\frac{5}{2}.\]

Add \(\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) to both sides:

\[x^2 - 3x + \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{5}{2} + \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{10}{4} + \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{1}{4}.\]

Write as a perfect square and take the square root of both sides:

\[\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = -\frac{1}{4} \implies x - \frac{3}{2} = \pm\sqrt{-\frac{1}{4}} = \pm\frac{i}{2}.\]\[x = \frac{3}{2} \pm \frac{1}{2}i.\]

question.en: [Quadratics & Complex Numbers · Practice 3] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 5t + 5 \), evaluate \( g(8) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 50 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 8 \): \( g(8) = 5(8) + 5 = \mathbf{45} \). Setting \( 5t + 5 = 50 \) gives \( 5t = 45 \implies t = \mathbf{9} \).

question.en: [Quadratics & Complex Numbers · Practice 4] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 6t + 6 \), evaluate \( g(10) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 72 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 10 \): \( g(10) = 6(10) + 6 = \mathbf{66} \). Setting \( 6t + 6 = 72 \) gives \( 6t = 66 \implies t = \mathbf{11} \).
